passage:
A city added shade structures over sidewalks near hospitals, bus stops, and schools. The project began after a heat study showed where pedestrians suffered most.
Some structures included solar panels that powered night lights. Others used plants.
Students helped survey people using the shaded routes. Many said they walked more comfortably and waited for buses with less stress.
Shade seemed simple, but it changed daily movement.
Urban comfort is not a luxury. It affects who can walk, wait, work, and travel safely. In a hotter world, shade becomes public health.
